authority.macro_body: return fn##_Init(EVP_MD_CTX_get0_md_data(ctx)); — no NULL test on ctx or md_data

defect.reachability: EVP_MD_meth_get_init (src/evp/digest.rs:1565; libcrypto.ld:1886) returns the callback to any C caller. A fresh EVP_MD_CTX_new() is zero-filled, so md_data is NULL; a NULL ctx dereferences NULL as well. The getter's documented contract says nothing about md_data, so the writable-block precondition was never established by the ABI.

reproduction.before_fix_candidate: cargo test --lib legacy_sha1_init -- --nocapture (court container): thread 'evp::legacy_sha::tests::legacy_sha1_init_refuses_context_without_md_data_and_inits_bound_context' panicked at core/src/ptr/mod.rs:702: 'unsafe precondition(s) violated: ptr::write_bytes requires that the destination pointer is aligned and non-null'; process aborted (SIGABRT, exit 101).
reproduction.before_fix_authority: Six one-process C probes against the pinned 3.6.4 install, three digests × {fresh EVP_MD_CTX_new(), NULL ctx}. Each printed md_data=(nil) (fresh) or ctx=NULL (null) and died with exit 139 (SIGSEGV) at the *_Init write.
reproduction.after_fix_candidate: The same focused tests return 0 for both fault shapes and 1 for the bound table path; the SHA1/SHA224/MD5(abc) vectors match.

fix.shape: Each of the three initialisers now calls a private init_md_data(ctx, owner, size) helper before writing. The helper refuses (returns None) when ctx is NULL, md_data is NULL, digest is NULL, or the context is bound to a different method whose ctx_size is smaller than the digest context; otherwise it returns the block. A refusal answers 0, the C initialise failure value, touching no memory.
fix.normal_path: A context bound to the callback's own table object, or to a method with ctx_size >= the digest context, still calls the authority's SHA1_Init/SHA224_Init/MD5_Init and returns its value. Digest maths and result values are unchanged.
fix.authority_comparison: §17 divergence, not compatibility: the authority performs the NULL write and faults. The crate does not reproduce UB; it returns 0 on exactly the shapes where the authority does not return.

mechanisms.name: legacy digest init callback md_data precondition
eliminated: the assumption that a C caller of the exported callback supplies a writable md_data
the assumption that a fresh EVP_MD_CTX carries a method/block that this callback may write
relocated: the remaining raw reads (ctx->md_data, ctx->digest, digest->ctx_size) and the *_Init write into init_md_data + the three callbacks, each with a # Safety contract

unsafe_ops.removed: none: the raw field reads and the external *_Init call still require unsafe; the unsafe expressions remain visible and documented
unsafe_ops.relocated: the unconditional SHA*_Init(md_data(ctx)) call is replaced by init_md_data(ctx, owner, size) + a validated pointer in all three initialisers
unsafe_ops.introduced: two private unsafe helpers (src/evp/legacy_sha.rs:121-159, src/evp/legacy_md5.rs:79-117), each with a # Safety contract; no new exported symbol, no new unsafe trait or safe interface

discharged: OSSH-DIS-018 sha1_init: the callback establishes and validates its SHA_CTX; C-valid contexts either have a writable block or are refused before the write
retained: A C-invalid pointer is outside the C contract (not a claim; the same boundary every exported pointer-taking entry point has).

The owner-table branch accepts a manually bound context with non-NULL md_data; the public API cannot construct that state (a fresh context has NULL md_data and EVP_DigestInit_ex rebinds the method before the callback), so it is not caller-reachable.
introduced: The helper's caller must pass a live owner method; the three call sites pass the static table address.
